item.text: {"gaps":[{"concept":"Precocious puberty begins before age 8 in girls or 9 in boys; delayed puberty means no breasts by 13 or testicular enlargement by 14.","why_tested":"Age and physical findings determine whether a vignette describes abnormal pubertal timing.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"In boys, testicular volume of at least 4 mL marks gonadarche; pubic hair alone does not establish true puberty.","why_tested":"Distinguishes early testicular maturation from isolated adrenarche.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"LH stimulates Leydig-cell testosterone production; FSH supports Sertoli cells and spermatogenesis and stimulates ovarian granulosa-cell aromatase.","why_tested":"Links gonadotropin changes to the source of pubertal sex steroids.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Sex steroids increase growth through GH–IGF-1; estrogen drives epiphyseal maturation and closure in both sexes.","why_tested":"Explains why early puberty initially accelerates growth but can reduce adult height.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Central precocious puberty follows the usual sequence with bilateral testicular enlargement; peripheral androgen excess may cause virilization without testicular enlargement.","why_tested":"An early-virilizing boy’s testicular size distinguishes central from peripheral puberty.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Hypothalamic hamartoma can cause central precocious puberty with gelastic seizures.","why_tested":"Episodes of inappropriate laughter accompany early pubertal development.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Familial male-limited precocious puberty (testotoxicosis) results from activating LHCGR mutations, producing testosterone despite suppressed gonadotropins.","why_tested":"A boy has familial early virilization and high testosterone with low LH.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"hCG-secreting tumors stimulate Leydig-cell LH receptors, causing testosterone-mediated precocity in boys despite suppressed pituitary LH.","why_tested":"A boy has elevated hCG, high testosterone, and low LH.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Granulosa-cell tumors secrete estrogen and can cause early breast development or bleeding; Leydig-cell tumors secrete androgens and cause virilization.","why_tested":"The sex steroid pattern identifies the tumor behind peripheral precocity.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"In 21-hydroxylase deficiency, elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone and adrenal androgens cause early pubarche with suppressed gonadotropins.","why_tested":"A child has early androgenic signs without gonadal maturation.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"McCune–Albright syndrome arises from a postzygotic mosaic GNAS mutation; autonomous ovarian estrogen production can cause episodic vaginal bleeding.","why_tested":"Recurrent bleeding and asymmetric skin lesions accompany gonadotropin-independent puberty.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Severe primary hypothyroidism can cause precocious breast development or bleeding with delayed bone age (Van Wyk–Grumbach syndrome).","why_tested":"Delayed skeletal maturation distinguishes this presentation from typical precocious puberty.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Premature thelarche has isolated breast development without accelerated growth or advanced bone age.","why_tested":"An otherwise well young girl has breast budding without progressive puberty.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Premature adrenarche causes pubic or axillary hair, body odor, and acne without breast development or testicular enlargement.","why_tested":"Early hair growth occurs while the gonadal axis remains prepubertal.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Pubertal gynecomastia reflects a transient increase in the estrogen-to-androgen effect during otherwise normal male puberty.","why_tested":"A pubertal boy develops bilateral breast tissue without other evidence of disease.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Hypogonadotropic delayed puberty has low sex steroids with low or inappropriately normal LH/FSH;
